headline: NASA's Curiosity Rover Discovers Vast Honeycomb Landscape on Mars
meta_description: After 14 years on Mars, NASA's Curiosity rover has found an extraordinary field of geometric polygon patterns stretching across Valle Grande.
summary_short: NASA's Curiosity rover has discovered an astonishing "sea" of honeycomb-like polygonal fractures covering a Martian valley, each pattern just inches wide.
body:
After fourteen years exploring Mars, NASA's Curiosity rover has stumbled upon one of its most striking discoveries yet: an enormous field of geometric polygon patterns stretching across a valley nicknamed Valle Grande. The honeycomb-like formations, each measuring between 1.5 and 3 inches across, cover the terrain in every direction, climbing even the sides of a nearby 20-foot-tall butte called Miraflores. The rover captured the full extent of the landscape in a 360-degree panorama on June 19 and 20, revealing patterns that continue as far as the camera can see. "We've seen a lot of fascinating landscapes through Curiosity's eyes, but this sea of polygons took our breath away," said Ashwin Vasavada, the mission's project scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

While Curiosity has encountered smaller clusters of similar geometric shapes before, this discovery presents a puzzle. Scientists believe several processes could have created these formations. Some polygons on Mars clearly began as cracks in drying mud, but repeated warming and cooling cycles can also fracture ground into geometric shapes. Underground compression may have forced water out of sediment, producing similar patterns. Researchers are now carefully studying the chemistry and structure of Valle Grande's formations to determine which process—or combination of processes—shaped this extraordinary landscape.

The discovery adds to Curiosity's remarkable fourteen-year legacy of transforming our understanding of ancient Mars. The rover has found evidence that billions of years ago, lakes and streams dotted Mount Sharp's lower foothills, leaving behind chemical traces including carbon-based molecules believed to be precursors to RNA and DNA. These findings confirm that ancient Mars once possessed the water, chemistry, and nutrients that could have supported microbial life.
quick_facts: Curiosity rover discovered honeycomb patterns in Valle Grande, Mars
Each polygon measures 1.5 to 3 inches (4 to 8 centimeters) across
Patterns cover a 20-foot-tall butte called Miraflores
Rover has been exploring Mars for 14 years since August 2012
Scientists studying whether patterns formed from drying mud or thermal fracturing
